chapter_title: Concerning the Five Saviours, the Resurrectors of

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
In that operation, living goods and truths are set within the forms prepared to receive them.

A second restoring operation is the Divine vitality that proceeds to reawaken what has fallen dormant.

A third restoring operation is the Divine Itself in first permanence, because by Divine truth all living goods and truths that have been dispersed are gathered back into unity and returned to the Divine; then they receive the form proper to their renewed state and enter peace.

A fourth restoring operation is enlightened understanding, because it illumines living goods and truths and turns them back toward the image of their own intended quality.

A fifth restoring operation for those who are in good is again the Divine Itself in first permanence and stability. It holds all subordinate powers bound together in one steadfast order, and remains unshaken in the inmost ground of permanence. It removes the covering that has been laid over them, and draws them into conjunction by the inward compulsion of Divine wisdom. Divine love becomes the measure of their willing, and by that measure they are re-established, raised into their proper order and function, and kept there until the process is brought to its completion.

paragraph_translations.translation: In that operation, living goods and truths are set within the forms prepared to receive them.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES the naming of restoring operations but begins mid-thought.
paragraph_translations.notes: The subject and prior operation are missing; “forms” is clear as recipient structures, but the larger sequence is truncated.

paragraph_translations.translation: A second restoring operation is the Divine vitality that proceeds to reawaken what has fallen dormant.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by naming the next means of restoration.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Living Spirit” is translated by function as proceeding Divine vitality; the specific action is not stated in the fragment.

paragraph_translations.translation: A third restoring operation is the Divine Itself in first permanence, because by Divine truth all living goods and truths that have been dispersed are gathered back into unity and returned to the Divine; then they receive the form proper to their renewed state and enter peace.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS with a clearer mechanism of restoration through Divine truth.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Father, the First Established One” is rendered as the Divine in primacy and stability; the phrase about “his word” requires reading as Divine truth ordering and gathering.

paragraph_translations.translation: A fourth restoring operation is enlightened understanding, because it illumines living goods and truths and turns them back toward the image of their own intended quality.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by shifting from gathering to illumination and reorientation.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Light Mind” is taken as enlightened understanding; the bracketed clause is partially preserved but still thin on process-detail.

paragraph_translations.translation: A fifth restoring operation for those who are in good is again the Divine Itself in first permanence and stability. It holds all subordinate powers bound together in one steadfast order, and remains unshaken in the inmost ground of permanence. It removes the covering that has been laid over them, and draws them into conjunction by the inward compulsion of Divine wisdom. Divine love becomes the measure of their willing, and by that measure they are re-established, raised into their proper order and function, and kept there until the process is brought to its completion.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS into a culminating act of stabilizing, unveiling, and reordering until completion.
paragraph_translations.notes: The repeated naming of the Divine as both third and fifth operation suggests either two distinct modes of the same source or a textual gap; “veil” is taken as obscuration or restraint that prevents right action.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Despite heavy truncation, the surviving lines hold together as a numbered sequence of restorative Divine operations: implantation into receptive forms, reanimation by proceeding vitality, recollection and re-forming by Divine truth, illumination by enlightened understanding, and final stabilization through conjunction with the Divine and ordered elevation. Coherence is strongest in paragraphs 4 and 6 where cause-and-effect is explicit; it stumbles where defining clauses are missing (especially paragraphs 2–3).

findings.diagnosis: Fragmentary start of a numbered correspondential sequence; the reader stumbles because the first item (the ‘first resurrector’) and its subject are missing, leaving only the tail of a functional clause about ‘forms’. This is a genuine lacuna, not a voice intrusion.
findings.evidence: Text is explicitly broken: “¶2: ... i]t therein [the lives are planted in their forms].” The spiritual reading notes: “begins mid-thought… The subject and prior operation are missing… larger sequence is truncated.” The clause itself teaches by function (implantation of lives into forms), but the numeral sequence cannot be reconstructed from what survives.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: a coherent sequence of restorative operations described by what each agent DOES (gathering by ‘word’, enlightening, binding/ordering, unveiling, drawing). The only ‘stumble’ (Father named again as third and fifth) is best explained by damage/ellipsis or a two-aspect presentation, not an administrative overlay or seam-expansion, because the paragraphs continue to teach by mechanism rather than by jurisdiction.
findings.evidence: Each unit is grounded in function rather than governance: ¶4 “because by his word shall all lives… gather in… receive… form… rest”; ¶5 “because [he enlightens… and turns them]”; ¶6 “He binds all the powers… unveil the veil… draws them… will is their measure… establishes them… stands them up [in their rank]… until [the completion].” The spiritual reading’s main hesitation is internal repetition: “The repeated naming of the Divine as both third and fifth operation suggests either two distinct modes… or a textual gap.” That is consistent with lacunae (noted throughout by brackets) and with the text’s sustained process-language; there are no jurisdiction lists, ranks of named rulers, or territorial administration typical of the administrative voice.

findings.diagnosis: Apparent ‘rank/order’ language is not an administrative insertion here; it is integrated into the correspondential mechanics of restoration (re-establishing powers into their proper functional order). The narrative flows without requiring a governance taxonomy.
findings.evidence: Potentially administrative-sounding phrase: “he stands them up [in their rank] there.” But it is embedded inside a causal chain of actions (“binds… stands firm… unveils… draws… will is their measure… establishes…”) that the spiritual reading successfully renders as a culminating stabilization. There is no accompanying list of offices/authorities or jurisdictional mapping; ‘rank’ functions as ordered state rather than bureaucratic roster.

textual_criticism.summary: No administrative overlay or seam-expansion is identifiable in the extant material. The chapter’s stumbling points arise from damage/lacunae (especially ¶2 and the thin, bracketed clauses), not from later administrative insertions. Recommendations: 0 excisions, 0 annotations, 3 no-action findings (including one damaged fragment and two clean correspondential continuities).

harmonized_paragraphs.text: ... i]t therein [the lives are planted in their forms].
The second resurrector is [the Living Spirit].
And the third resurrector is the Father, the First [Established One], because by his word shall all lives [that are scattered] gather in and go to him, and they receive [their own form] and rest.
The fourth resurrector is the Light Mind, because [he enlightens the lives and turns them toward their likeness]. ⟨p.46⟩

The fifth resurrector to the good [lives] is the Father, the First established one [in his firmness]. [He binds] all the powers, and he stands firm [in the root of his stability]. He shall unveil the [veil] over them [that was spread], and he draws them to him [by the attraction of his light], his will [is their measure], and he [establishes] them, and he stands them up [in their rank] there, and they remain until [the completion].

changes_summary: No changes made. All findings (1–3) recommended none (no excisions or annotations), identifying the stumbling points as lacunae/damage rather than later insertions.
